question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

Scarcely had I left when it **was starting** to rain.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the conjunction "**Scarcely**," which is typically followed by an auxiliary verb, such as "**had**," in the past perfect tense.
 
• The structure of the sentence requires parallel construction, and the correct verb form after "**had**" is the past participle "**started**."
 
• The phrase "**was starting to rain**" is incorrect because it does not align with the past perfect tense required in the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase is "**had started to rain**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Scarcely had I left when it started to rain."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "had started"** – While this option uses the past perfect tense, it disrupts the logical sequence of events in the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "was begun"** – This option is grammatically incorrect because "was begun" is passive and inappropriate here.
 
• **Option 3: "did start"** – This option is incorrect as it introduces unnecessary emphasis and does not fit the structure of the sentence.
